_comment: Every URL pattern and selector the solver detects and drives a captcha with.
This file is the default: PageSolver (Python) and CaptchaKraken (JS) load it
when no other is given. To add your own, write a file of the same shape and
pass its path (or the parsed object) as `selectors` in PageSolverConfig
(Python) or CaptchaKrakenConfig (JS). A file of your own may hold only what
it changes: `custom`, any vendor under `vendors` (it replaces that vendor's
whole entry), or any list under `generic`; the rest comes from this file.
custom: your own entry, for a captcha the built-in vendors do not know. It
is detected before every built-in vendor and reported as `unknown`, and its
submit, text box, refresh and slider controls are tried before the generic
ones. It must name a `widget`, `challenge` or `checkbox`; `hosts` is optional.
detector: the element detector that finds grids, tick boxes and pieces on the
CPU before any model is asked. `standard` (ResNet-18, 124 MB), `lite`
(MobileNetV3, 24 MB, ~6x faster on one CPU) or `auto`: lite on two usable
CPUs or fewer, and above that standard only when a one-off timing predicts
it inside 200 ms a board. Only the chosen model is downloaded.
CAPTCHA_KRAKEN_DETECTOR_MODEL overrides this.
vendors: one entry per vendor, in detection order. Order matters: the driver
takes the first visible match in table order. `hosts` are URL substrings of
the vendor's code on the wire; every other field is a list of CSS (or
Playwright `xpath=`) selectors, except `response`, `checked`, `accepted` and
`fresh` (one selector each), `banners` ([selector, verdict] pairs) and
`hold_completes` (true or false). `note` is for people, not the solver.
generic: the fallbacks tried after every vendor's own. `submit_text` is the
button text probed for a submit control, in order.
Keys starting with `_` are comments. Field reference: `_fields`.

_fields.hosts: URL substrings of the vendor's code on the wire. A tripwire, not a detector: the host stays on the wire when a vendor renames its markup (see TRIBAL_KNOWLEDGE.md). BotDetect is self-hosted, so it has none.
_fields.challenge: On the host page: the open challenge. Detected first.
_fields.checkbox: On the host page: the checkbox. Detected while `response` is empty and `checked` is not showing.
_fields.enclave: On the host page: a frame the vendor draws its other frames inside. Every host-page selector also reads the inside of a visible one.
_fields.widget: On the host page: inline widget shapes, detected last. Iframe selectors go first; a class that lives inside the frame document (.CheckboxCaptcha, .mtcap) only ever matches an inline embed.
_fields.response: On the host page: the field the vendor fills on success. Read first and unconditionally, because hCaptcha's overlay hides the anchor.
_fields.checked: Inside the checkbox frame: the box shows accepted. Demo pages do not always fill `response`.
_fields.box: Inside the checkbox frame: the box itself, clicked from the DOM. A vendor without one is found on a photograph. An in-page checkbox that names one is a button with no tick box to find, and is clicked where it is.
_fields.accepted: On the host page: the vendor painted its success state. Visibility is part of the test (see TRIBAL_KNOWLEDGE.md).
_fields.fresh: Inside the challenge frame: a new round has painted, with text.
_fields.images: Inside the challenge frame: the pictures a board is made of; the driver waits for each to have painted.
_fields.submit: Inside the widget: the vendor's own submit control, tried after the generic text probes.
_fields.banners: Inside the challenge frame: verdict banners and what each means.
_fields.blocked: Inside the challenge frame: the vendor refusing to serve this client at all. Nothing after it can succeed.
_fields.passive: On the host page: the vendor's frames that are never interactive, so a page showing only these has no widget.
_fields.text_input: Inside the widget, and its enclosing fieldset/form: the answer box of a typed captcha.
_fields.slider_handle: Inside the widget: the knob a slide must start on; a drag from the piece moves nothing.
_fields.piece: Inside the widget: the piece, measured to steer the slide and dragged directly when there is no track.
_fields.refresh: Inside the widget: the control that deals a new puzzle, pressed when the model answers `refresh`.
_fields.hold_completes: A press-and-hold that completes on its own once full, and resets when let go before it has: the fill reaching the answer's `to` is not a release, and the hold lasts until the widget says it is done.

recaptcha.note: An Enterprise sitekey serves the same widget from /recaptcha/enterprise/ instead of /recaptcha/api2/.

hcaptcha.note: Keyed on the `hcaptcha` substring, not the apex host: challenges are served off newassets.hcaptcha.com. secure-api.js draws every frame inside a full-viewport enclave, one per render, and only a visible one holds an open challenge.

geetest.note: v4's "Click to verify" bar opens the puzzle. Its container wears `geetest_freeze_wait` while the puzzle is open (`geetest_boxShow` only until a first wrong answer, after which the box stays up dealing a new one) and `geetest_success` once passed, so the checkbox matches only a bar that has not been clicked yet.

tencent.note: Both in-page and iframe shapes stay (Tencent moved in-host on 2026-08-11; see TRIBAL_KNOWLEDGE.md), and the iframe id is prefix-anchored: `[id*=tcaptcha]` also matched MTCaptcha's iframe and hid that `.mtcap` matched nothing.

human.note: The press-and-hold widget. Found by its host-page container whether the button is drawn inline or in the vendor's iframe inside it: the hold is performed on a photograph of the container, so it never needs the frame's DOM.

awswaf.note: The card is drawn in an open shadow root, which the locator engine pierces; its Confirm is found by the text probe.

captchafox.note: The puzzle opens in a modal over the "I am human" box, which stays on screen, so the modal is a challenge: a widget would be outranked by the box and the box clicked again.

dingxiang.note: Every mode opens the same popup card. The trigger bar under it has no box to tick and is not a widget.

funcaptcha.note: The host page carries the outer frame (iframe.arkoselabs.com/<key>/index.html) and the game is two frames inside it; the game frame's own path is listed so a page that frames the game directly is found too.

proton.note: Proton frames its own captcha at /core/v4/captcha, on account-api.proton.me or under the app's own /api/.
